weather_reasons: NWS hourly forecast includes thunderstorm potential

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 301224
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
524 AM MST Fri Oct 30 2026

.UPDATE...Updated Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A Flood Watch remains in effect for portions of south-central 
  and eastern Arizona today.

- Showers and thunderstorms, some producing moderate to heavy 
  rainfall, are expected today focused over South-Central Arizona.
  Localized rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are likely. 

- A few strong to marginally severe thunderstorms are possible
  today, especially from late morning into the afternoon, with 
  the main hazards being large hail and damaging winds.

- A followup weather system Saturday night through Sunday night
  will bring even better moisture over the region and result in a
  prolonged period of light to moderate rainfall, leading to
  additional flooding concerns. Thus, a Flood Watch will also be
  in effect Saturday night through Sunday night for much of 
  Central and Eastern Arizona. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Midlevel water vapor imagery reveals an elongated subtropical jet
streak, stretching from near Hawaii to just off the Baja 
California Coast. A broad area of upper level divergence is 
apparent downstream of this feature and especially to the east of 
a rather compact shortwave that has developed off the 
SoCal/Northern Baja Coast. Meanwhile, a period of southerly flow 
and strengthening 850-700 mb southerly jet has pulled better 
atmospheric moisture into the area, resulting in ensemble mean 
PWATs surging upwards of 200-250% of normal overnight. An area of 
showers and storms had already developed over Southeastern AZ 
yesterday evening which progressed northward, reaching the Phoenix
area in the early morning hours. This area of showers and storms 
well out ahead of the compact shortwave is feeding on a surge of 
higher theta-E and coincident elevated instability (RAP analyzed 
MUCAPE between 500-1000 J/kg), which is easily released by the 
upper level divergence apparent in the upper air objective 
analysis. Latest CAM guidance does indicate this early 
shower/storm activity will be transient and clear north and east 
of the Phoenix area over the next few hours, however, small 
disturbances or strong enough outflow from this initial activity 
may be enough to continue redeveloping activity through the rest 
of the morning. The next area for shower/storm development this 
morning may well be over Southwest AZ, near/east of the Lower CO 
River and coinciding with the nose of the 850-700 mb south 
southeasterly jet. Some top-down moistening of the lower levels 
will continue to occur through the rest of the morning over 
portions of the forecast area, especially with any shower/storm 
activity that develops, setting the stage for a lower DCAPE 
environment that will also be conducive to higher rain rates (less
sub-cloud evaporation). The highest rain rates and best coverage 
of showers and thunderstorms is likely to occur during the late 
morning through the early evening with the compact shortwave and 
its axis of relative vorticity moving east/northeastward across 
South-Central AZ. Average rain totals between 0.50-1.00" centered 
over and just north and east of Phoenix are still forecast. Away 
from the foothills/higher terrain of Central AZ, forecast rain 
totals drop off quickly. However, localized amounts of up to 
around 2" are definitely possible with any severe or training 
storms, including over portions of the Greater Phoenix Area. With 
the expected totals, a Flood Watch remains in effect for Maricopa 
County and portions of NW Pinal County starting this morning, then
expanding into Gila County by the afternoon. 

Another concern through early this evening will be the potential 
for marginally severe hail and damaging winds with some of the 
stronger thunderstorms that do develop. Forecast soundings 
indicate effective bulk shear upwards of 20-30 kts, even as much 
as 40 kts during a narrow winds of time as the shortwave moves 
through South-Central AZ late this morning into this afternoon. 
Instability will, however, be a limiting factor. MUCAPEs upwards 
of 500-1250 J/kg are already present this morning, and 500 mb 
temperatures around -12C are certainly supportive of the large 
hail potential, but midlevel lapse rates look like they gradually 
deteriorate through the rest of the day, leading to declining 
instability. 00Z GFS bufr sounding now only show around 250 J/kg 
MLCAPE this afternoon. This could also be due to poor surface 
insolation due to increased cloud cover over previous model runs. 
Nevertheless, the environment should support some rotating 
updrafts, which could produce marginally severe hail and localized
strong to severe wind gusts with some of the strongest storms 
today (most likely late this morning through mid afternoon).

As the shortwave departs the area late this evening, rain chances
will drop off dramatically, and much of the area should remain 
dry through much of the day on Saturday. Some lingering, scattered
showers may persist over upslope/higher terrain areas of Central 
AZ, as southwesterly flow remains elevated on Saturday ahead of 
the broader troughing off the West Coast. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...    
By late Saturday evening, conditions begin to align for a longer 
duration and more widespread rainfall event through Sunday. The 
aforementioned subtropical jet streak is shown by global guidance 
contracting and cyclonically curving around the base of the broader 
troughing off the West Coast, as it begins to progress eastward. 
Strong dynamical ascent mechanisms and a prolonged period of 
southwesterly upslope flow over the Central AZ high terrain will 
align with excellent, deep moisture through the atmospheric column. 
Impressively high PWATs are still forecast, in excess of 1.00-1.25" 
and near the maximum of climatology for early November. NAEFS/ENS 
mean IVT values are consistent with an inland penetrating 
atmospheric river and are also, unsurprisingly, near climatological 
maximum values for the time of year (peaking around 300-600 
kg/(ms)). However, midlevel lapse rates will be poor and thus 
instability will be very limited, with MUCAPEs likely never 
exceeding 200-300 J/kg. We expect showers to blossom first over the 
high terrain northeast of Phoenix sometime in the evening Saturday 
before filling in across most of south-central Arizona around or 
just after midnight. Showers will stay somewhat scattered through 
the overnight hours before becoming widespread over much of Arizona 
by mid morning Sunday. As the main shortwave begins to track through 
southern California later Sunday morning, a fairly solid shield of 
light to moderate rain should move through southern California and 
then through Arizona Sunday afternoon. Upslope showers should 
persist over portions of south-central Arizona into the high terrain 
into Sunday evening, but the activity should be gradually winding 
down.

Expected rainfall rates on Sunday are not all that high, but rain 
totals will add up over time as this event will last longer than our 
typical weather events. Based on the record moisture levels, strong 
forcing, but little instability rainfall rates will generally be in 
the 0.1-0.2"/hr range in the Phoenix area to as high as 0.2-0.3"/hr 
in the high terrain north and east of the Phoenix area. Fairly 
steady light to moderate rainfall is expected from just before 
sunrise through the afternoon in the aforementioned areas with 
rainfall totals averaging 1-1.5" in Phoenix to 2-3" over the higher 
terrain. Believe it our not, the NBM is also suggesting the 
possibility (25%) of rainfall totals over 2" in the Phoenix to as 
much as 3-4" in the high terrain. Much lower rainfall totals of 0.25-
0.5" are expected over the lower deserts of southwest Arizona and 
southeast California due to some rain-shadowing effects and the lack 
of upslope forcing.

Even if the average forecast rainfall totals come to fruition on 
Sunday, the bulk of the rain will runoff as it will be falling on 
already saturated soils. In turn, another Flood Watch has been 
issued for a large area of south-central AZ, and the eastern AZ high 
terrain starting overnight Saturday night and lasting into early 
Monday morning. During this time we anticipate the potential for 
many of the washes filling or overflowing, and flooding in some of 
the larger creeks and rivers as all of the expected rain works 
through the water basins.

Dry air will begin to filter into the region from the northwest 
later on Sunday, overspreading the bulk of the area by Monday 
morning. We may have some lingering showers across the eastern 1/3rd 
of Arizona Sunday night into Monday morning, but additional rainfall 
amounts should be fairly light. The rest of Monday will bring 
decreasing clouds as the drier air works into the region while 
another follow-on shortwave trough moves southeastward into northern 
New Mexico. Temperatures for both Sunday and Monday will be fairly 
cool with highs as low as the lower 70s for the Phoenix area to 
maybe the mid to upper 70s across the western lower deserts. Upper 
level ridging is then forecast to mostly take over across the Desert 
Southwest going into the middle part of next week, but temperatures 
will be fairly slow to rise with readings staying below normal.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1224Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT; 
Periods of sub-VFR CIG & VIS and VCSH/VCTS will be the primary
aviation impact today through this afternoon before conditions
improve heading into tonight. Early morning showers have been
mostly staying off to the E and NE of terminals. There will remain
a 20-30% chance for VCSH/VCTS this morning, but best chances
(50-90%) will be this afternoon, mainly between 19-02Z, and this
will also be the timeframe with the highest potential for sub-VFR
conditions. Lingering VCSH cannot be ruled out tonight and
scattered clouds will persist with bases around 4-5K ft AGL.
E-SE winds will prevail through most of the TAF period with speeds
mostly at or below 10 kts. Some variability and a period of W-NW
winds may develop this afternoon with VCSH/VCTS.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No significant aviation weather impacts are expected through the
TAF period. SHRA/TSRA is forecast to stay east of the Colorado
River this morning, but brief VCSH/VCTS cannot be ruled out at
KBLH (10% chance). At KIPL, westerly winds will prevail throughout
the period while at KBLH, winds will generally fluctuate between
the southeast to southwest with periods of light variability early
this morning. Overall speeds will remain aob 10 kts with the
exception of KIPL early this evening as temporary peak gusts
upwards of 20-25 kts are likely. SCT-BKN mid to high level cloud
decks along with FEW to occasionally SCT decks around 4-6K ft will
be common through this afternoon. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Showers and thunderstorms will impact portions of the eastern 
districts today with heavy rainfall likely in some areas, followed
by a lull in rain chances on Saturday. Minimum humidities will
range between 30-70% areawide today and Saturday and improve 
further on Sunday, following excellent overnight recoveries. After
the lull on saturday, chances for rain increase again Saturday
night followed by widespread light to moderate rainfall on 
Sunday areawide. Outside of any thunderstorms, winds will remain
generally between 10-20 mph and favor southeasterly to southerly
directions through the weekend. Conditions will gradually dry out
next week as the unsettled pattern departs and temperatures
moderate closer to seasonal normals, however, humidities will 
remain above 25% areawide, and temperatures will still remain in a
slightly below normal category.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...     Flood Watch from Saturday evening through late Sunday night for 
     AZZ534-537>563.

     Flood Watch through this afternoon for AZZ534-537>551-553>555-
     559.

     Flood Watch from noon MST today through this evening for AZZ552-
     556>558-560>563.

CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock
LONG TERM...Whittock/Kuhlman
AVIATION...Benedict/Lojero
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock
